README.md:50:State and browser secrets use 32 random bytes each. Five-minute state records contain only hashes, role and expiry. The browser cookie is HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax, Path=/; HTTPS uses Secure and the `__Host-` prefix. It is cleared after callback. Starting another flow in the same browser replaces the cookie; complete one connection at a time.
README.md:66:The target remains **Cloud Run scale-to-zero + Firestore**, not Cloudflare. Memory state/auth stores are explicit tests/development choices. `NODE_ENV=production` requires `STATE_STORE=firestore`, `GOOGLE_CLOUD_PROJECT=raid-relic-hackathon`, and complete OAuth/webhook settings. Unknown stores/projects or emulator configuration are rejected; SDK or store failures never silently fall back to memory. SDK construction passes the exact project ID. No cloud credentials are provisioned or read by this run. A future authorized cloud runtime would need its operator-managed identity and Firestore access.
README.md:68:The store interface supports atomic event acceptance, ritual reads, create/consume OAuth state, encrypted token reads, and lease-protected token writes. Firestore acceptance transactionally writes event dedupe and ritual/chat mutation together. The fake tests enforce reads before writes, rollback on commit failure, retried transaction callbacks, concurrent duplicate delivery and one-use state across service instances. These tests do not prove real SDK/emulator/database behavior.
README.md:70:OAuth expiry and event replay expiry are checked in application transactions; physical document cleanup/TTL policies are not configured. Firestore currently retains expired records until an operator adds retention cleanup. Latest chat metadata is bounded per configured host. Memory OAuth state has a capacity limit and lazy expiration; memory resets lose state, grants and rituals. Firestore key paths hash external IDs to prevent path injection. OAuth tokens are application-encrypted, while state hashes, role metadata and account/chat IDs are not secret ciphertext.
